To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel USY@Zno/Al2 O 3 catalyst was prepared through an in situ growth strategy, in which the USY crystals were coated with a ZnAl-LDHS layer that was transformed into ZnO/Al 2 O 3 upon calcination.
we developed a facile method to prepare a USY@Zno/Al2 O 3 material with unique properties and excellent catalytic activity for the Baeyer-Viliger oxidation of ketone with H2 O 2 as an oxidant.

we have successfully developed an efficient Lewis acid catalyst for the Baeyer-Viller oxidation of ketones by combining the unique Lewis acidity of ZnO and Al2 O3 and hierarchical porosity of a USY@ZoO/Al2O3 composite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of a novel core-shell structured catalyst that combines the advantages of both the zeolite and metal oxide.

the preparation of a new class of Lewis acid catalysts with controllable acidity and hierarchical porosities for Baeyer-Villerger oxidation of ketones, which is of great importance in the development of sustainable and green chemical processes.
the preparation of USY@Zno/Al2 O catalysts by in situ growth of ZnAl-LDH on USY zeolites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work has demonstrated the feasibility and potential of a novel in situ growth method for the preparation of ZnO/USY@Al2 O3 catalysts, which are highly active and stable for the Baeyer-Viliger oxidation of ketone with H2 O.

a USY zeolitewith an external ZnO phase was prepared via in situ growth of a ZnAl-LDHS phase on the zeolite surface, which upon calcination gave rise to a core-shell USY@ZNO/Al2 O 3 catalyst with promising performance for the Baeyer-VilIiger oxidation of ketone.

the USY@ZNO/Al2 O 3 materials were prepared via the facile one-pot in situ growth of ZnAl-LDH on the surface of USY zeolites followed by calcination and were demonstrated as efficient catalysts for Baeyer–Villiger oxidation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the USY zeolitewas used to confine a ZnAl-LDHS phase and then to form a USY@Zno/Al2 O 3 composite, which gave rise to the formation of unique Lewis acid centers and a hierarchical porous structure.
the USY zeolitessurface was used as an ideal template for the in situ formation of a ZnAl-LDHS phase, which was transformed into a controllably confined ZnO/Al 2O 3 phase upon calcination.
the USY@Zno/Al2 O 3 catalysts are promising for the oxidation of ketones to esters, which are important precursors for the synthesis of fine chemicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in situ growth of a ZnAl-LDHS phase on the surface of an USY zeolites can be readily achieved by a facile method that benefits from the interaction of an added Zn source and the Al species extracted from the USY zeo-lite crystals.

the unique Lewis acidity of the USY@Zno/Al2 O catalysts was attributed to a strong interaction between the ZnO/Al 2 O3 composite and the USY zeoite, which was beneficial to the activation of H2 O2 and bulky tert-butylhydroxide.
the USY zeolin is not only a good host for the confinement of ZnO nanoparticles but also an excellent precursor for the formation of a Lewis acid catalyst.
